candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p.13 / PDF p.17
candidate.educational_objective: Interpret creatinine together with eGFR as markers of kidney filtration without overclaiming a specific diagnosis.

options.A: The pattern is consistent with reduced glomerular filtration and warrants clinical evaluation of kidney function
options.B: The pattern proves improved kidney filtration
options.C: Creatinine and eGFR have no role in assessment of kidney function
options.D: A high creatinine value alone identifies a specific cause of kidney disease

candidate.rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories uses serum creatinine with eGFR to diagnose and monitor kidney disease and estimate glomerular filtration. Creatinine is removed largely by glomerular filtration; however, creatinine alone is imprecise and is influenced by factors such as muscle mass. A rising creatinine with declining eGFR supports reduced filtration but does not identify the cause by itself.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Supports creatinine/eGFR for kidney-function assessment and the inverse relationship between creatinine and filtration, with important limitations of creatinine alone.
candidate.source_document_title: Creatinine with Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR), Serum (CRTS1)
candidate.stem: An adult's serum creatinine has increased while the reported eGFR has decreased from prior values. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
